newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia police arrest 109 Timorese after brawls.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia police arrest 109 Timorese after brawls.

text.p: Indonesian police said on Friday they had arrested 109 youths in East Timor for taking part in brawls between young Catholics and members of a military-backed group earlier this month.

"We have arrested 109 people after mass brawls in Viqueque on February 7 and 8. I can confirm there was some trouble there, but there were no fatalities," East Timor's deputy police chief Lieutenant-Colonel Atok Rismanto told Reuters by telephone from the East Timor capital, Dili.

The brawls were the latest reported incidents in East Timor since December 24 when a crowd welcoming Nobel peace laureate Bishop Carlos Belo back to Dili attacked police and killed a local soldier in the cathedral grounds.
At least 15 people were arrested in connection with the Christmas Eve disturbances.

Church sources in Viqueque, about 100 km (60 miles) southeast of Dili, said the latest trouble erupted after members of the military-backed Gada Paksi youth organisation attacked 10 Catholic youths, a priest and his driver on February 7.

"The Gada Paksi members beat the priest and the youths because they accused them of trying to have an illegal meeting. Fights between the two groups continued until February 9," said one church source.
The source said there were reports that some Catholic youths were shot and wounded in the ensuing fights and added none of the Gada Paksi members had been detained.

Rismanto denied police had opened fire on demonstrators. "We only fired warning shots. No one was hurt in the incident," he said. Rismanto declined to give other details, but said the situation was under control in Viqueque.
Church sources said many Catholic youths in Viqueque had fled the regency to avoid arrest.

Gada Paksi, the Youth Guard of Integration Upholders, was set up in 1995 and its members receive military-style training in Java. East Timorese residents have accused members of the group of intimidating people who oppose against the territory's integration with Indonesia.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and made it its 27th province a year later in a move not recognised by the United Nations.

"In my letter I said that if they failed to agree, all things that had been discussed between related parties with the mines and energy department were not valid," Sudjana said.

Indonesia said last November it wanted Bre-X to partner Barrick, and the Mines and Energy Ministry said in December they had agreed to split Busang, with 22.5 percent going to Bre-X, 67.5 percent to Barrick and the rest to the government.

Indonesia's Nusamba group, 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by President Suharto and 10 percent each by timber baron Muhammad "Bob" Hasan and Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto, has bought a 50-percent stake in two companies with minority interests in two of the Busang areas.
Barrick has an alliance with a company controlled by Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardijanti Rukmana.
